definition: Optuna is an open-source Python library for automatic hyperparameter tuning of machine learning models.
details: It was first introduced in 2018 by Preferred Networks, a Japanese startup that works on practical applications of deep learning in various fields. The beta version of Optuna was released at the end of the year, with the subsequent first major stable release announced in January 2020.

explainer.lead: How to install Optuna, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
import optuna
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score
from sklearn.svm import SVC

X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)

def objective(trial):
    c = trial.suggest_float("C", 1e-3, 1e3, log=True)
    return cross_val_score(SVC(C=c), X, y, cv=3).mean()

study = optuna.create_study(direction="maximize")
study.optimize(objective, n_trials=30)
print(study.best_params)

explainer.inAi: Tune learning rates, LoRA ranks or retrieval settings automatically; Optuna prunes bad trials early to save GPU time.
explainer.jsNote: Optuna is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.
